Two widely-used frameworks were considered for implementation: caffe and pytorch. caffe was selected as it offers a well-documented and user-friendly interface for developing and deploying neuralnetwork-based solutions, particularly for applications involving image-processing and computer-vision. Pytorch was also considered, but it required more extensive configuration and customization to meet the specific requirements of our application. Ultimately, caffe provided a more streamlined and efficient solution for our particular use-case, enabling us to focus our efforts on model development and optimization without having to spend excessive time on framework-specific implementation details.
Another important consideration involved the design and configuration ofthe recurrent network architecture itself. Various configurations were explored to find the optimum balance betweenthe model's capacity to capture complex patterns in data while ensuring computational feasibility and scalability. Different combinations of hidden-layer sizes, activation functions and recurrent-cell types were tested to identify the configuration that yielded the highest performance while remaining computationally efficient. LSTM cells were found to offer superior capabilities in capturing and retaining longterm dependencies, thus making them an ideal choice for modeling sequences of varying lengths and complexities.
Hyperparameter optimization was another critical aspect that required careful attention during implementation and experimentation. Multiple hyper parameters were systematically tuned and evaluated to optimize the learning process and improve the overall accuracy of predictions.
